stems.name: Software Requirements and Problem Definition
stems.description: Knowledge structure concerned with understanding software problems and stakeholder needs, defining system expectations, and establishing requirements that can guide subsequent engineering decisions.

stems.name: Software Architecture and System Structuring
stems.description: Knowledge structure concerned with organizing software-intensive systems at a high level and reasoning about components, interfaces, architectural decisions, system qualities, constraints, and engineering trade-offs.

stems.name: Software Design and Construction
stems.description: Knowledge structure concerned with transforming requirements and architectural structures into implementable software through abstraction, decomposition, detailed design, programming, integration, and disciplined construction practices.

stems.name: Software Verification, Validation, Testing, and Quality
stems.description: Knowledge structure concerned with establishing whether software satisfies its intended requirements and quality expectations through verification, validation, testing, review, analysis, measurement, and quality assurance.

stems.name: Software Security, Reliability, and Dependability
stems.description: Knowledge structure concerned with engineering trustworthy software systems capable of operating under faults, failures, threats, misuse, uncertainty, and changing operational conditions.

stems.name: Software Evolution and Lifecycle Engineering
stems.description: Knowledge structure concerned with software as a continuously changing engineering artifact across development, delivery, operation, maintenance, adaptation, modernization, and retirement.

stems.name: Configuration, Integration, Delivery, and Operations
stems.description: Knowledge structure concerned with maintaining software integrity across versions and environments while integrating, releasing, deploying, observing, and operating software systems reliably.

stems.name: Software Engineering Processes, Models, and Methods
stems.description: Knowledge structure concerned with systematic ways of organizing, representing, performing, evaluating, and improving software engineering work across different development contexts.

stems.name: Software Engineering Management and Economics
stems.description: Knowledge structure concerned with planning, coordinating, estimating, measuring, and making software engineering decisions under constraints of resources, schedule, uncertainty, risk, cost, and value.

stems.name: Human, Collaborative, and Professional Software Engineering
stems.description: Knowledge structure concerned with software engineering as a human and professional activity involving collaboration, communication, ethical responsibility, stakeholder interaction, engineering judgment, and societal consequences.

stems.name: Computational, Mathematical, and Engineering Foundations
stems.description: Foundational knowledge structure supporting software engineering reasoning by connecting computation, mathematical reasoning, systems thinking, measurement, and general engineering principles.

operations.reason: The two structures form a continuous transformation from detailed software design into implementation and integration while remaining separable at the knowledge-scope level.

operations.result: Software Verification, Validation, Testing, and Quality
operations.reason: Testing is treated as part of a broader assurance structure rather than as an isolated implementation activity.
These areas share a continuous concern with software integrity and controlled transition across versions, environments, releases, and operational states.
Trustworthiness represents a cross-lifecycle engineering concern substantial enough to remain a distinct Stem rather than being absorbed into testing or quality.
